text:
maya: heads up — p99 latency on inference API jumped ~3x starting ~02:15 UTC. only saw after last night's infra deploy (kernel 5.18.* + CUDA 12.2 drivers). support tickets coming in. we should triage asap
ron: seen it too. p95 also up but p99 worse. chart: cpu low, gpu util fine, but NVMe tail latency spikes match timeline. scoped to eu-west cluster so far. :eyes:
sre-oncall: @maya can you attach the grafana panel link? and any customer ids affected?
maya: https://grafana.internal/r/ABCD123 — look at p99 tokens latency for model-group-prod. customer A and two others reported timeouts.
lina: throwing NVMe iostat and dmesg from one host — copied below:

```
# iostat -x 1 5
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s    wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz  await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.00   3.00  1536.00   24.00   13.20    0.10   0.83   0.80   1.25   0.20   2.40
nvme0n1         10.00  200.00   128.00  2048.00  40.80    2.45  150.20  120.50  220.30  1.00  80.00
```

[dmesg excerpt]
```
nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 12 timeout, resetting controller
blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
```

kevin: looks like controller resets correlated with CUDA driver unload/reload on deploy. kernel upgrade pulled in a newer nvme driver that interacts oddly with our GPU PCI resets.
eng-bot: deploy #2026 completed 2024-11-09T02:05:43Z — kernel 5.18.12 -> 5.18.15, cuda-driver 12.2.0 -> 12.2.3 applied to eu-west pool
support-lead: customers hitting 504s. raising P1. need quick mitigation plan, even if workaround.
ron: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback kernel/drivers on a canary set, 2) route traffic away from eu-west to us/eu-other (capacity permitting), 3) enable fallback model variant on cheaper infra to lower GPU-reset surface.
sre-oncall: routing can be done but will increase latencies globally. rollback is heavy. can we isolate by hosttag and cordon nodes with NVMe errors?
maya: cordon/evict on hosts reporting nvme resets seems safest immediate move. I've flagged ~8 nodes. starting evict now.
lina: collecting nvme-cli smart log and nvme fw-log for the reset hosts. attaching snippets:

```
# nvme id-ctrl /dev/nvme0
mn: INTEL SSDPE2KX040T7
fr: E2102A6
```

kevin: interesting — firmware E2102A6 on these drives. we recently onboarded a batch with the new FW. possible firmware/driver clash.
ron: triage checklist I'm putting together:
- reproduce on staging: try same kernel+driver+fw combo, run synthetic KV-style IO while running inference workload.
- collect host logs: dmesg, nvme-cli smart-log, nvidia-smi -q, syslog, kernel oops if any.
- check PCI reset frequency: `grep -i reset /var/log/dmesg`
- bisect by rolling back either kernel patch or driver to identify culprit.

sre-oncall: for mitigation timeline: cordon + route traffic within 15min; if that stabilizes, continue draining and repro; else prepare rollback.
maya: cordoned hosts, traffic shifted ~5% to other regions. p99 dropped by ~30% but still elevated.
kevin: we should also try disabling PCIe ASPM for a test host — sometimes power management interacts. command: add `pcie_aspm=off` to kernel boot args and reboot one node in canary.
lina: note: customers seeing timeouts sometimes accompanied by `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT` in our logs — suggests GPU-side hangs when NVMe resets occur. full log block:

```
[worker-123] ERROR inference_runner: model inference failed: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runner.py", line 412, in run
    ctx = session.run(inputs)
RuntimeError: CUDA kernel launch timeout
```

support-lead: send status to impacted customers: "we are investigating infra-level storage resets post-OS/driver deploy; short-term mitigation applied (cordon + traffic shift)."
ron: next steps for root cause: reproduce on isolated lab with same HW + nvme fw, try 12.2.3 driver + kernel 5.18.15; if repro -> file bug with NVMe vendor & NVIDIA; if not repro -> run targeted kernel bisect with our micro-patches.
kevin: I'll start repro job on lab cluster with stress-ng + gpu-bench and background fio. will log timestamps and enable PCIe tracing.
sre-oncall: please also enable per-node tracing: `echo 1 > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/tracing_on` and capture `trace_pipe` around event window.
maya: small mitigation we can script now: if NVMe reset count > 3 in last 10m, mark host as degraded and route away automatically. I can PR the checker to ops playbooks.
lina: posting collected logs to s3://redwood-incidents/2412345678/ — nvme-smart, dmesg, nvidia-smi, inference logs.
eng-bot: alerting channel #eng-runtime with `:triage:` for follow-up post-mitigation.
kevin: ETA for repro job 45m. I'll update thread with findings.
sre-oncall: if rollback path chosen, coordinate windows with infra release team — potential downtime for batch - will need exec signoff.
support-lead: keeping customers updated. thanks everyone. :pray:
maya: update 20: repro on lab succeeded: after ~2000 concurrent inference requests + fio in background we trigger nvme controller reset and GPU kernel timeouts. suspect interaction between nvme driver resets and CUDA 12.2.3 handling of PCIe device reset.
kevin: filing vendor bug with logs and reproduction steps. temporary plan: avoid simultaneous heavy host-local IO during peak inference by moving checkpointing and other IO to remote storage or staggered windows.
ron: summary for postmortem: cause — interaction of new kernel + nvme firmware + CUDA driver causing NVMe controller resets under mixed IO+GPU workload; impact — elevated p95/p99 and some 504s; mitigations — cordon/evict, route traffic, disable ASPM test, lab repro, vendor bug, automated degraded-host marking.
maya: will open incident postmortem doc and assign owners for each action item. closing thread for now — will post updates in #incidents when vendor responds.
